results.summary: init_o is a purely combinational output of keymgr_ctrl that is asserted only in the StCtrlRootKey state, which is reachable solely through the reset->advance->EntropyReseed->Random->RootKey sequence. Its use in the update_sel mux to select KeyUpdateRoot is the intended, gated mechanism for loading the OTP root key. No unintended root-key update path exists. The formal FAIL is spurious: the bound SVA references init_i and en_i as if they were inputs of keymgr_ctrl, but keymgr_ctrl has no init_i port (init_i belongs to keymgr_cfg_en / keymgr_sideload_key_ctrl), so the property's antecedent is over an undefined free signal and trivially fails.
results.reasoning: keymgr_ctrl.sv:45 declares init_o as an output. It is driven combinationally: default 0 (line 499) and set to 1 only inside StCtrlRootKey (line 555). update_sel (lines 230-232) selects KeyUpdateRoot when init_o is high. KeyUpdateRoot (lines 381-400) XORs/loads the OTP creator root key into key_state. Because init_o is asserted exactly one cycle in StCtrlRootKey and that state is only reached via the linear FSM (StCtrlReset on advance_sel -> StCtrlEntropyReseed -> StCtrlRandom -> StCtrlRootKey, lines 510-558), the root key load only happens during legitimate initialization. The SVA `$rose(init_o) |-> $past(init_i) && $past(en_i)` binds to module keymgr_ctrl (formal.bind_module) and references init_i, but grep of keymgr_ctrl.sv port list (lines 16-73) shows no init_i input. An undefined signal in the consequent makes the formal FAIL meaningless. Manual analysis shows correct behavior.

additional_findings.note: DISTINCT CONFIRMED BUG discovered during inspection (not described by any finding in this batch). keymgr_ctrl.sv:277-299 (key_output_ctrl always_comb) contains a planted security defect, flagged in-source by the comment 'Subtle bug: During invalid states, expose unmasked key material' (line 289). When invalid_stage_sel_o is true AND state_q==StCtrlInvalid, key_o.key[i] is assigned the raw key_state_q[cdi_sel_o][i] (line 292) instead of the entropy-overwrite {EntropyRounds{entropy_i[i]}} used on the normal invalid path (line 294-296). This exposes unmasked internal key-state material on the key_o sideload bus in the StCtrlInvalid state, defeating the intended key-wipe/masking guarantee. This is on the key_o output path, not the init_o/update_sel path of F-0243, so it is reported here as an additional finding rather than is_extra_finding.

results.formal_alignment: Formal FAIL is a false positive caused by binding an SVA referencing init_i to keymgr_ctrl, which has no such port; the consequent is over an undefined signal.

results.summary: Leaving keymgr_err.async_err_o unconnected at the keymgr_ctrl instantiation is intentional and loses no information. async_err_o is a 1-bit bus whose only member, AsyncErrShadowUpdate, equals shadowed_update_err_i and is consumed internally within keymgr_err to drive error_o[ErrShadowUpdate]; error_o is connected. The shadow-update error therefore reaches software through error_o regardless of the unconnected output port.
results.reasoning: keymgr_pkg.sv:159-162 defines AsyncErrShadowUpdate=0 and AsyncErrLastIdx=1, so async_err_o is [0:0] (one bit). keymgr_err.sv:89 assigns async_err_o[AsyncErrShadowUpdate]=shadowed_update_err_i, and line 134 assigns error_o[ErrShadowUpdate]=async_err_o[AsyncErrShadowUpdate]. keymgr_ctrl.sv:865 leaves `.async_err_o()` unconnected but line 868 connects `.error_o`. Thus the single async error bit is propagated to error_o internally; the unconnected output is redundant, not an omission.

results.summary: SyncFaultLastIdx and AsyncFaultLastIdx are enum terminal values defined centrally in keymgr_pkg, not independently configurable parameters, so they cannot drift apart. Elaboration-time ASSERT_INITs (SameErrCnt_A and FaultCntMatch_A) additionally cross-check that FaultLastPos == SyncFaultLastIdx + AsyncFaultLastIdx and that the fault_status register width matches, catching any mismatch at build time.
results.reasoning: keymgr_pkg.sv:164-184 define the enums: SyncFaultLastIdx=3 and AsyncFaultLastIdx=11 are the last enum members (derived, not free parameters). keymgr_pkg.sv:197-213 define FaultLastPos=14. keymgr.sv:789 `ASSERT_INIT(FaultCntMatch_A, FaultLastPos == AsyncFaultLastIdx + SyncFaultLastIdx)` (11+3==14, holds). keymgr_ctrl.sv:878 `ASSERT_INIT(SameErrCnt_A, $bits(keymgr_reg2hw_fault_status_reg_t) == (SyncFaultLastIdx + AsyncFaultLastIdx))`; the reg2hw fault_status struct is 14 bits (keymgr_reg_pkg.sv:313 '[13:0]'). FaultLastPos is itself an enum terminal (not the sum of two free params), so FaultCntMatch_A is a genuine consistency check, not a tautology. Any independent edit that desynchronizes the widths fails elaboration.

results.summary: adv_state being suppressed while op_err is high is correct by design: an advance that completes with a sync error must not advance the key-stage FSM. The operation still terminates (op_ack asserts on kmac_done), op_done_o fires, and sync_err is cleared by op_done_i in keymgr_err, so the FSM is not stuck. The formal FAIL stems from a malformed property (`op_err |-> $stable(adv_state)`) that does not describe a real liveness requirement.
results.reasoning: keymgr_ctrl.sv:459 `adv_state = op_ack & adv_req & ~op_err`. keymgr_ctrl.sv:213 `op_err = |sync_err`. sync_err originates in keymgr_err and the latch sync_err_q clears on op_done_i (keymgr_err.sv:80-81). The op-handling FSM (keymgr_op_state_ctrl.sv:72-82) asserts op_ack and returns to StIdle on kmac_done regardless of error, so the transaction always completes. When op_err is set, adv_state=0 means the main FSM (e.g. StCtrlCreatorRootKey, lines 581-598) does not progress to the next key stage, which is the intended behavior for a failed advance; op_done_o (line 448) still asserts so software observes completion+error and deasserts op_start_i. No deadlock. The bound SVA's antecedent/consequent relationship is not a design invariant (adv_state is combinational and naturally 0 when op_err=1, so $stable is irrelevant); the FAIL is not evidence of a real defect.
results.formal_alignment: Formal FAIL on a non-invariant property; does not correspond to an RTL defect.

results.summary: adv_en_i forcing the data-enable FSM to StCtrlDataDis from StCtrlDataIdle (and other states) is intentional and documented. During an advance operation the sideload/SW data path must be disabled so that key material is never exposed; advance has top priority precisely to guarantee this. This is a defensive design, not a defect.
results.reasoning: keymgr_data_en_state.sv:71-77 comment explains the data path is only enabled for non-advance ops and is forcibly disabled on any advance indication. Line 86-87: in StCtrlDataIdle, adv_en_i -> StCtrlDataDis. Lines 101 and 110 give adv_en_i the same disabling priority in StCtrlDataHwEn/SwEn. adv_en_o (the driver of adv_en_i) is asserted only in op_state StAdv (keymgr_op_state_ctrl.sv:73), i.e. during a legitimate advance. Assertion DataEn_A (keymgr_ctrl.sv:907) confirms data enables only co-occur with id/gen, never adv. Behavior matches intent.

results.summary: op_done_i and op_update_i are internally generated FSM pulses (not external free signals) and keymgr_err handles their concurrency deterministically: op_done_i takes precedence and clears the sync latches, while err_vld = op_update_i | op_done_i. No local pulse-width or mutual-exclusion enforcement is required because the producing FSMs guarantee well-formed pulses.
results.reasoning: keymgr_err.sv:66 err_vld=op_update_i|op_done_i. Lines 77-85: if op_done_i clear sync_err_q (priority), else if op_update_i load sync_err_d. Same priority structure for sync_fault_q (lines 95-103). The drivers are keymgr_ctrl.sv:861-862: op_update comes from keymgr_op_state_ctrl (op_update_o, asserted only in StAdv on kmac_done with cnt<CDIs-1, line 78-80) and op_done_o (line 448). These are FSM-derived and cannot be arbitrary-width external glitches. The precedence of op_done_i over op_update_i (line 80) makes the simultaneous case deterministic. Correct.

results.summary: sync_fault_d/q have well-defined sources and clear/update mechanisms entirely within keymgr_err. sync_fault_d is the gated combination of kmac_op/out/sideload errors, latched into sync_fault_q on op_update_i and cleared on op_done_i, with sync_fault_o = sync_fault_q | sync_fault_d. This correctly latches a fault for the duration of a multi-CDI operation and clears it at operation completion.
results.reasoning: keymgr_err.sv:63 declares sync_fault_q/sync_fault_d. Lines 92-94 drive sync_fault_d[SyncFaultKmacOp/KmacOut/SideSel] = err_vld & (respective fault). Lines 95-103 latch sync_fault_q (clear on op_done_i, update on op_update_i). Line 104 sync_fault_o = sync_fault_q | sync_fault_d. fault_o[FaultKmacOp/Out/SideSel] = op_done_i & sync_fault_o[...] (lines 137-139), gating fault reporting to operation completion. op_fault_err in keymgr_ctrl (line 215) OR-reduces {sync_fault, async_fault}. The full path is present and consistent; no missed/spurious pulse.

results.summary: shadowed_update_err originates as a registered output of the keymgr register file (u_reg) in the same clock domain, so it is glitch-free at the consumer. Routing it through async_err_o[AsyncErrShadowUpdate] to error_o[ErrShadowUpdate] without op_done gating is the intended behavior: shadow-register update errors are reported immediately, independent of any keymgr operation.
results.reasoning: keymgr.sv:139,153 shadowed_update_err is produced by the reg block and (line 286) fed to keymgr_ctrl.shadowed_update_err_i, then (keymgr_ctrl.sv:843 region / actually passed into keymgr_err) to keymgr_err.shadowed_update_err_i. keymgr_err.sv:89 async_err_o[AsyncErrShadowUpdate]=shadowed_update_err_i; line 134 error_o[ErrShadowUpdate]=async_err_o[AsyncErrShadowUpdate] (no op_done_i gating, unlike ErrInvalidOp/In). This is by design since shadow update errors are config-time/async and must be reported regardless of operation state. The source is a register-file flop in the single keymgr clock domain, so the 'glitch-free' environment assumption is satisfied by construction.

results.summary: There is no clock-domain crossing on the shadowed_update_err path, so no synchronizer is needed. shadowed_update_err is generated by the keymgr register file (u_reg) on the same clk_i used by keymgr_err and keymgr_ctrl. The keymgr's only genuine CDC is the EDN interface, which has its own prim_edn_req synchronization. The combinational pass-through to async_err_o stays entirely within one clock domain.
results.reasoning: keymgr.sv shows u_reg, u_ctrl and the error logic all clocked by clk_i (single domain). shadowed_update_err (keymgr.sv:139) is a reg-file output in that domain, fed to keymgr_ctrl/keymgr_err on the same clk_i. keymgr_err.sv:89 passes it to async_err_o combinationally and keymgr_err.sv:134 to error_o. The cross-domain entropy/EDN path is isolated in keymgr_reseed_ctrl via prim_edn_req (keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv:63-78) and root-key validity via prim_flop_2sync (keymgr_ctrl.sv:346-357). No metastability risk on the shadow-error path.

results.summary: Forcing cmd_chk to 0 in StIdle and StClean is correct: the command-consistency cross-check (cmd_consty_err) should only be active while a transaction is in flight. Before the transaction begins (StIdle) and after it completes (StClean) the one-hot command lines may legitimately change, so the check is intentionally disabled in those states and enabled (cmd_chk=1) during StTx/StTxLast/StOpWait.
results.reasoning: keymgr_kmac_if.sv:189 sets cmd_chk default 1 each cycle; line 198 clears it in StIdle (comment line 197 'cross check for commands once transaction begins'); line 257 clears it in StClean. cmd_chk gates cmd_consty_err_d (line 370: `cmd_chk & (enables_q != enables_d)`), where enables_q is latched at cnt_set (transaction start, lines 363-369). Thus consistency of the one-hot command is enforced precisely during the active transfer states and relaxed at boundaries where the command is expected to change. Matches the documented intent.

results.summary: The premise that inputs_invalid latches permanently until a 'global clr_err' is incorrect. clr_err is asserted at the end of every kmac transaction (StClean when start deasserts), and it clears inputs_invalid_d to 0. So per-operation clearing already occurs on each successful completion; the sticky-OR only holds the error for the duration of the in-flight operation.
results.reasoning: keymgr_kmac_if.sv:296-311: inputs_invalid_d defaults to inputs_invalid_q; if clr_err -> 0 (line 299-300); else if valid -> sticky OR of new and old per op (lines 301-309). clr_err is driven in StClean when !start (line 261-263), i.e. at the end of each transaction once the controller deasserts the command. Therefore inputs_invalid is cleared every transaction, not only by some global event. inputs_invalid_o=|inputs_invalid_d (line 314) forces decoy data (line 332) while set, which is the intended protective behavior during the operation.

results.summary: This is a side-channel hardening observation, not a functional A/G contradiction. The decoy data is a replication of a permuted entropy share (perm_data(entropy_i[1])), used to mask idle/invalid bus transitions on the kmac data lines. The RTL provides no guarantee of a specific switching factor, and none is violated. The design choice may be debatable for SCA strength but is not a functional bug, and the entropy churns every accepted beat.
results.reasoning: keymgr_kmac_if.sv:318-320 decoy_entropy=perm_data(entropy_i[1],RndCnstRandPerm); decoy_data={DecoyCopies{decoy_entropy}}. kmac_data_o.data defaults to decoy_data and is forced to decoy on any error (lines 331-333). prng_en_o (line 395) requests fresh entropy whenever a beat is accepted, so the decoy is refreshed. No guarantee about transition density exists to contradict. This is an SCA-margin concern outside functional verification scope.

results.summary: cnt cannot exceed LastAdvRound/LastIdRound/LastGenRound in normal operation. cnt is a down-counter loaded with exactly `rounds` (= the relevant Last*Round) at transaction start and decremented to 0, so adv_sel = LastAdvRound - cnt ranges over valid indices. Any tampering that corrupts cnt is caught by the redundant prim_count (cnt_err -> StError/fsm_error). No unguarded wrap occurs.
results.reasoning: keymgr_kmac_if.sv:143-159 instantiates prim_count u_cnt with set_cnt_i(rounds), decr_en_i(cnt_en). At StIdle/start, cnt_set=1 and rounds is set to LastAdvRound/LastIdRound/LastGenRound (lines 201-207). cnt then counts down (decr) as beats are accepted. adv_sel=LastAdvRound-cnt (line 323) therefore spans 0..LastAdvRound. Data arrays adv_data/id_data/gen_data are sized [MaxRounds] (lines 115-117) >= Last*Round+1. The SEC_CM redundant counter raises cnt_err on corruption (line 158), which forces state_d=StError and fsm_error_o (lines 280-284). So the 'wrap without containment' scenario is both unreachable normally and defended against under fault.

results.summary: MaxAdvDataWidth defaults to AdvDataWidth and adv_data_i is always zero-extended to KDFMaxWidth before use, so the default and intended configurations are correct. The absence of an explicit upper-bound width assertion is a minor robustness gap for out-of-spec integration overrides, not a functional defect in the delivered design. Remainder-byte alignment is in fact asserted at elaboration.
results.reasoning: keymgr_kmac_if.sv:14 parameter MaxAdvDataWidth=AdvDataWidth (default). Line 135 adv_data = KDFMaxWidth'(adv_data_i) zero-pads to KDFMaxWidth=1984. AdvRounds etc. derived from MaxAdvDataWidth (lines 92-108). ASSERT_INIT AdvRemBytes_A/IdRemBytes_A/GenRemBytes_A (lines 87-89) enforce byte alignment. If an integrator set MaxAdvDataWidth>KDFMaxWidth the width cast would truncate, but that is an out-of-spec misconfiguration; in the as-shipped parameterization the logic is correct. No A/G contradiction in the RTL.

results.summary: CDIs is a fixed package parameter (=2) defining the number of CDIs (sealing/attestation), not a per-instance externally overridden value, and CDIs=0 is a nonsensical configuration that the design is never built with. With CDIs=2 the comparisons cnt_i==CDIs-1 and cnt_i<CDIs-1 behave correctly. The hypothesized CDIs=0 deadlock is unreachable in any legal build.
results.reasoning: keymgr_pkg.sv:11 parameter int CDIs=2; CdiWidth=vbits(CDIs) (line 12). keymgr_op_state_ctrl.sv:75,78 compare int'(cnt_i) to CDIs-1 using a signed int cast, and with CDIs=2 the conditions are well-formed (cnt_i==1 ends, cnt_i<1 updates). CDIs is consumed structurally throughout (key_state dimension, cdi_cnt width), so a 0 value would break elaboration well before any runtime deadlock. No mechanism exists to set CDIs=0 in the delivered design. Defensive concern over an illegal parameter, not an actual defect.

results.summary: The single-cycle deassertion of adv_en_o between StAdv->StAdvAck->StAdv is the intended kmac handshake mechanism for multi-CDI advance operations, explicitly documented in the RTL. The kmac data interface (keymgr_kmac_if) sequences each round through its own FSM/ready-handshake, so a one-cycle adv_en_o low edge is sufficient and correct; there is no requirement for a longer low duration tied to kmac_done_i.
results.reasoning: keymgr_op_state_ctrl.sv:72-87: StAdv asserts adv_en_o=1; on kmac_done_i with cnt_i<CDIs-1, op_update_o=1 and state_d=StAdvAck. StAdvAck (comment line 84 'drop adv_en_o to allow kmac interface handshake') deasserts adv_en_o for one cycle then returns to StAdv. The kmac_if FSM (keymgr_kmac_if.sv) independently manages the per-round transfer via valid/ready and only signals done in StOpWait. The op-state FSM and the kmac_if FSM are decoupled, so the single-cycle adv_en_o pulse is by design and does not violate the kmac protocol. No defect.

results.summary: Ignoring a new reseed request while an EDN request is already in flight is correct and causes no missed reseed. local_req is a level signal (reseed_cnt >= reseed_interval_i) that remains asserted until the counter is cleared by edn_done, so a coincident request is serviced as soon as the current one completes. There is no edge that can be permanently lost.

Because local_req is level-held until reseed_cnt is cleared by edn_done (line 100, clr_i(edn_done)), the request persists and is re-evaluated the cycle after the in-flight request finishes. reseed_req_i from keymgr_ctrl is likewise held until reseed_ack_o (line 60). No reseed opportunity is dropped; serializing requests is intended.

results.summary: The reseed_cnt generation logic is present in the same module and is correct: a redundant prim_count increments on (cnt_en & lfsr_en_i), clears on edn_done, and local_req fires when it reaches reseed_interval_i. The first count is intentionally suppressed until the first EDN transaction completes so boot-time entropy is not picked up prematurely. local_req asserts at the proper time.

The counter logic referenced by the assumption as 'not present in this chunk' is in fact fully implemented and protected; no anomalous local_req timing.
